properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 15 at 10:58AM CDT until October 15 at 12:45PM CDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
At 1058 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have
fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 2 to 3 inches in 1 hour. Flash
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Midland, Midland International Air and Space Port, Midland Airpark
and Warfield.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Midland Draw and Monahans Draw.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Fire Weather Watch issued October 15 at 10:51AM CDT until October 17 at 8:00PM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA
properties.description:
...CRITICAL FIRE WEATHER CONDITIONS POSSIBLE SATURDAY...

.A strong cold front will quickly move through the area Friday
afternoon. The front will be mostly if not completely dry as it
moves through the area. Quickly after it moves into the Gulf much
drier air will surge in behind it. In addition cooler air will
move in along with strong northerly winds. On Saturday sunny skies
and winds in the first 1500-3000 ft will be out of the same
direction sllowing for efficient mixing. This will help to bring
wind gusts of 15 to as high as 30 miles an hour across most
locations along and north of I-10. This will also lead to even
drier air mixing into the area helping to drop the RH into the
mid to lower 30% range with some locations seeing the relative
humidity just below 30%. This will combine with current D1 and D2
drought conditions across all of southwest Mississippi and much
of southeast LA along and northwest of a line from Thibodaux to
Franklinton. This could provide ample fuel for wildfires. The
combination of breezy to gusty winds, current drought conditions,
ample fuel, and very dry conditions will allow any fire that
develops to spread quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.

* AFFECTED AREA...Pointe Coupee, West Feliciana, East Feliciana,
St. Helena, Washington, Iberville, West Baton Rouge, East
Baton Rouge, Assumption, St. James, Wilkinson, Amite, Pike,
Northern Tangipahoa, Walthall, Southeast St. Tammany, Northern
St. Tammany, Southwestern St. Tammany, Central Tangipahoa,
Lower Tangipahoa, Northern Livingston, Southern Livingston,
Western Ascension and Eastern Ascension.

* WINDS...North 10 to 15 mph with gusts up to 30 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 30 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Fire Weather Watch means that critical fire weather conditions
are forecast to occur. Listen for later forecasts and possible
Red Flag Warnings.

properties.headline: Gale Warning issued October 15 at 7:51AM AKDT until October 15 at 10:00AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Gale Warning, southeast winds 30 to 40 kt with
gusts up to 45 kt and seas 22 to 27 ft. For the Small Craft
Advisory, south winds 25 to 35 kt with gusts up to 40 kt and
seas 18 to 23 ft expected.

* WHERE...Cape Edgecumbe to Cape Spencer out to 15 NM.

* WHEN...For the Gale Warning, until 10 AM AKDT this morning.
For the Small Craft Advisory, until 4 PM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.
properties.instruction:
Mariners should alter plans to avoid these hazardous conditions.
Remain in port, seek safe harbor, alter course, and/or secure the
vessel for hazardous conditions.

properties.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued October 15 at 7:51AM AKDT until October 15 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the first Small Craft Advisory, southeast winds 25
to 35 kt with gusts up to 40 kt. For the second Small Craft
Advisory, south winds 15 to 25 kt with gusts up to 35 kt
expected.

* WHERE...Northern Chatham Strait.

* WHEN...For the first Small Craft Advisory, until 4 PM AKDT
this afternoon. For the second Small Craft Advisory, from 7 AM
to 10 AM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft.
properties.instruction:
Inexperienced mariners, especially those operating smaller
vessels, should avoid navigating in hazardous conditions.
